value.assumption_check: ONE LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION IS STILL UNSTATED AND IT IS NAMED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: that a third-party harness accepts an arbitrary base_url for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Measured so far is only that hermes-agent supports OpenAI, OpenRouter, Anthropic and local providers and switches with `hermes model`. The build's FIRST act is to check that config surface, because if it is absent the seam is still right and its first consumer is not hermes. A second assumption, weaker: that OpenAI chat-completions shape maps onto the domain request without loss — roles and multi-turn message arrays have no counterpart in a single canonical prompt string, so the translation is where loss would hide.
value.builder_check: Wearing the cheapest-builder hat, these are answered so nobody infers them at build time. (1) WHERE: a machine under cairn/devices/inference_domain/machines/, not a new device and not a tool — it is glue over an existing primitive. (2) IT OPENS NO SOCKET: it calls domain.resolve(); if a builder reaches for httpx or requests, that is the wrong turn and import_sieve will say so. (3) WHAT SERVES IT: RULED AND CLOSED 2026-09-11 — the door opens its OWN service port and does not route to web_server. Akien: 'the web server rule was because during theigors, you were creating seperate web servers on port after port for each device. akien hereby allows the exception because this is not the User Interface web server, this is a service port.' The one-web-server rule governs the USER INTERFACE, not sockets: a UI surface faces a person and arrives as a declared pane; a service port faces a machine. The test is who is on the other end. This port exists because a third-party harness can only be configured with a base_url — a measured constraint of the consumer, not a builder convenience. It may NOT serve HTML to a human at that port; that would be the TheIgors failure exactly. Ruling: CairnCommons/decisions/2026-09-11-the-one-web-server-rule-governs-the-ui-not-service-ports.json. WAS: undecided and it matters — an HTTP listener is needed for a base_url to point at, and this system's standing rule is one web server with surfaces in the shim, never a device with its own server. THIS IS THE ONE QUESTION A BUILDER CANNOT ANSWER ALONE and it routes to web_server's owner, not to a fresh listener. (4) TRANSLATION LOSS: OpenAI sends a messages array with roles; the domain canonicalizes a request. The mapping must be deterministic and total, because canonicalization is what the cache keys on — two different message arrays flattening to one canonical string would serve one agent another agent's answer. (5) SHAPE OF THE ANSWER BACK: OpenAI's response envelope carries usage counters, and the domain already returns real cost and provenance additively, so the counters are available rather than fabricated. Do not invent them.
value.collision_check: Checked the compile-once thesis (Telos 1) and it is a DISTINCTION, not a collision. The why of each side: compile-once exists so a SETTLED answer is not re-bought; an agent's retry is by definition asking for an UNSETTLED one. They are not exclusive, and the store already carries a per-answer horizon, so zero is a legal value rather than a carve-out. Also checked Law 6 sole-path: composing domain.resolve() rather than opening a socket means this ADDS no door, and import_sieve enforces that at proof and build time. Recorded distinction: inference_domain has anticipated a second protocol OUTBOUND (the gemini residue); this is the first inbound one.
value.falsifier_check: The intent's falsifier stands and is checkable at three named instruments: (a) an unmodified harness completes a multi-turn session; (b) every call lands BOTH an inference_calls row and an emission line in ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/, joined by canonical digest — this is the exact agreement tooth an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started already implements, so the instrument exists; (c) a byte-identical retry returns a fresh sample. HORIZON: the first real multi-turn agent session. Wrong-intent tell: the adapter needing its own host connection, which import_sieve would red at proof time without anyone having to notice.
value.missing_check: Yes, one point was asserted wrapped and is not. The intent says 'a zero-horizon lane for interactive agent traffic' as though the lane's SELECTOR were settled; it is not. What distinguishes agent traffic from any other caller — an explicit request field, a domain vertical row in stacks/domains.json, or the OpenAI door itself always requesting horizon zero — is undecided. My read, recorded so the builder is not left guessing: the door requests it, because the door is the thing that knows its callers are agents, and a request field would let any caller opt out of compilation which is the whole thesis. Not ratified.

value.better_approach: Two smaller ways, both looked at and both rejected on measurement. (a) Make the agent speak ollama instead — that requires editing the agent, which is precisely the cost this whole direction exists to avoid (922MB .git, upstream at PR #107,000, a permanent merge burden). (b) Stand a translating proxy up OUTSIDE inference_domain — rejected because it would be a SECOND thing that dials a host, which is the exact breach Law 6 and import_sieve exist to prevent. Inside the domain is not the elaborate option, it is the only one that does not open a door.
value.hidden_assumption: That hermes-agent — and harnesses generally — accept an arbitrary base_url for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. UNVERIFIED. What is measured is only that it supports OpenAI, OpenRouter, Anthropic and local providers and switches with `hermes model`. If an arbitrary base_url is not reachable through its config, this intent's value falls back to whatever other harnesses allow, and the seam is still right but its first consumer is not hermes.
value.prior_art: Consulted the compiled model after poking recompile_gate.sh: grep over CairnCommons/intentions-congruency-lab for openai / wire format / base_url returned ZERO. Nearest standing art is inference_domain's own filed residue that 'the gemini transport does not exist yet' — a second protocol on the OUTBOUND side, already anticipated. This is the same idea turned around to face INBOUND, which is a distinction to record rather than a collision.
value.real_collision: None terminal. The nearest is the compile-once thesis itself (Telos 1): a lane that must return a fresh sample on identical bytes LOOKS like an exemption from compilation. It is not — it is a HORIZON OF ZERO, and a per-answer horizon is already a field the store carries. The why of each side agrees: compile-once exists so a settled answer is not re-bought, and an agent's retry is by definition asking for an UNsettled one. Distinction recorded.

the_split.548dd13fb4db (this ticket): inference_domain carries a tool-using conversation. No wire format, no listener, no port. The layer below — built and proved first.
the_split.NEW: cairn/machines/openai_wire: a MACHINE, not a device and nobody's property: translate.py (pure OpenAI body <-> canonical request, answer <-> chat-completions envelope, tool_calls arguments JSON-string <-> object both ways) and serve.py (an HTTP handler composed with an INJECTED resolve callable — opens no socket at import, dials no host). Injection is what makes 'anybody can include it' true rather than aspirational, and it is the shape domain.resolve(request, *, resolver=...) already stands on.
the_split.cb97524c0e8e: hermes_shim holds openai_wire, injects the bus call to inference_domain, and owns the port choice, the fence, and ~/.hermes/config.yaml.

value.what_was_wrong: The cast put an OpenAI-shaped LISTENER on inference_domain — a second inbound wire format on the device. That gives the device two doors, so a mind arriving cold at inference_domain has to work out which door a call came through before anything else makes sense. The shim pattern already standing at cairn/devices/aider_shim keeps ALL foreignness at the edge: holder.py holds the foreign tool's surfaces, fence.py bounds what it may ask, translate.py speaks both tongues, and no other device has ever heard of aider. CC read 'openrouter interface' as an OUTBOUND provider (Cairn dialing openrouter.ai) and filed it in constrain's `out` bounds; it is INBOUND — the face a shim presents to hermes.

named_falsifications.claim: the survey's holdings, which are what the build COMPOSES
named_falsifications.finding: THE BIG ONE. The survey never held device.py's request whitelist — and that whitelist is where the ticket's own clause (a) was actually broken. The sweep found host.py (the Python call) and stopped, because the phrase 'the one door' was read as the resolver rather than as the BUS VERB every other device reaches it through. The chart leg at fault is SURVEY: `sought` did not point the light at the bus seam at all. Downstream this cost more than an edit — hollow's subject set is drawn from the decompose berth, so device.py was also invisible to the hollow reading (now cast as 39966e1cefe4).

named_falsifications.claim: the survey's absences, which are what the build may BUILD
named_falsifications.finding: The survey did not list the WATCHME probe as an absence, so the ticket's own watch berth was built outside the measured-absent set. It was legitimate work — the ticket's string carries WATCHME and the gate refuses an unarmed one — which is the point: a mandatory artifact the survey cannot see means the survey is not sweeping the ticket's workflow string.

It cited a ticket under a name that had since been renamed, and it was written BEFORE Akien's rescope, so its `out` list still fenced off a door the rescope had moved rather than deleted. Bounds authored before a rescope are stale by construction; the chain has no way to say so.
